items.title: US inflation set to cool in October after two months of sharp increases | World News - Business Standard
items.excerpt: 8 min read Last Updated : Nov 08 2026 | 1:03 PM IST By Vince Golle and Craig Stirling Prices for US goods and services probably rose at a slower pace in October after two particularly uncomfortable months for American consumers. The consumer price index is seen rising 0.3% after a 0.6% increase that was the largest since April, based on the median projection in a Bloomberg survey of economists ahead of Tuesday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics’ release. The core measure, which excludes often-volatile energy and food components, also probably cooled. The survey median sees a 0.2% increase for October, which would be the smallest advance in three months. The agency won’t publish year-over-year figures after it skipped the October 2025 CPI release due to the federal government shutdown at the time. ## The Fed is expected to hold rates steady. Warsh will have to explain why ## Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook The October CPI will be the last before the Federal Reserve’s meeting in December, at which investors expect policymakers to boost interest rates. Economists will also assess the finer details of the report for clues on inflation risks into early 2027. Economists at Citigroup Inc. said in a recent note that they anticipate limited pass-through of high energy costs to goods prices, as well as moderate services inflation. What Bloomberg Economics Says... > “We expect headline CPI slowed to 0.25% in October (vs. 0.65% prior). The core likely softened to 0.24% (vs. 0.33% prior), with both softer goods and services price gains driving the improvement. For goods, used cars and consumer electronics — categories that have faced pressure from the AI boom — saw slower inflation. For services, gains in owners’ equivalent rent are down a third from a September spike.” > > > > —Anna Wong, Troy Durie and Eliza Winger The latest snapshot of inflation also follows Friday’s stronger-than-expected October jobs report. Sustained employment growth has the potential of ensuring consumers keep spending, while allowing the Fed to keep its focus squarely on inflation. Another price report, due on Friday, is projected to show nagging inflationary pressures faced by companies. The producer price index is forecast to accelerate to 6.6% for the year through October, the steepest annual increase in nearly four years. items.title: Fed policymakers consider rate hike after strong jobs report - The Korea Herald
items.excerpt: Published : Nov. 8, 2026 - 10:24:06 ... A stronger-than-expected US jobs report bolstered the case for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, which had lost some momentum ‌amid a post-election stock market selloff and growing fears that weaker AI-driven demand could undercut the economy. Employers added 165,000 jobs last month, more than twice what economists had expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday, and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1 percent. Average hourly wages gained 3.1 percent from a year earlier, not enough to keep up with a 3.7 percent rise in consumer prices that is ‌taking a bigger chunk of the typical paycheck's purchasing power. After the US central bank left its policy rate on hold last month, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said policymakers would be watching for "the accumulation of data" to help decide whether more monetary policy tightening would be needed. For San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly, the latest monthly jobs report appeared to put a definitive tick in the "yes" column. "People are just at the point where they're — they say 'Inflation — I'm doing well ⁠in everything, except I can't keep up with inflation,' so that has to be our number one priority, and the fact that we have a solid labor market gives us the latitude, really, to just get that job done," Daly said in an interview on CNBC. "My expectation is, we're going to have to tighten policy further," said Daly, who is not a voting member of the Fed's policy committee this ⁠year but typically voices views similar to the majority view. Noting "how volatile the world seems to be in many ways," she added, "those volatilities are something that you have to take into account, collect more information, and be deliberate but more gradual in how you get there when you don't know exactly where you're going to need to head. But more is likely to be ​needed and certainly we're prepared — I'm prepared — to do that, if that's what the economy calls for." In comments at a St. Louis civic event Friday, St. ‌Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said inflation remained the top concern in his conversations with businesses in his district. "Inflation is a regressive tax, a distortionary tax," said Musalem, who has advocated for further rate ‌increases. "The best thing we can do for growth ‌and employment is bring inflation back down on a timely basis." He did not address a recent swoon in stock markets driven lower by new doubts about ‌the pace and sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom, but said for now he feels the emerging ​industry is feeding higher inflation through demand for commodities such as copper. Even if that pays off in future profit and productivity, "we need to make monetary policy for the economy of the day, not what it may be ⁠five years from now," Musalem said, and on that basis, for now at least, AI investment "will continue to contribute to inflation." ... The ‌release of the latest employment report, however, put a Fed rate hike back in focus. Markets were pricing about an 80 percent chance of a quarter-percentage-point policy rate increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, up from about 67 percent Thursday. Traders now also see the next and final rate increase coming earlier, in April instead of June, as the central bank battles inflation that has been running above its 2 percent target for more than ​five years. "This is a very strong labor market report on the heels of solid GDP and consumer spending data last week, reinforcing the economy's positive momentum," Olu Sonola, an analyst at Fitch Ratings, wrote after the report. Recent concern over AI poses a risk to that outlook, Sonola said, "but for now the economy remains on firm footing. The labor market's resilience keeps the Fed focused on inflation and pushes the policy debate further toward a December rate hike."

items.title: PCE inflation accelerates to 3.6% as GDP growth beats estimates, jobless claims fall – Trade Talk Journal
items.excerpt: November 8, 2026 US inflation accelerated in September, while economic growth exceeded expectations in the third quarter and jobless claims remained near multi-decade lows, presenting the Federal Reserve with a challenging policy outlook. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, the central bank’s preferred inflation gauge, increased 0.5% month-on-month on a seasonally adjusted basis, taking the annual rate to 3.6%, according to Commerce Department data released Thursday. The monthly increase matched the Dow Jones consensus forecast, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below expectations. Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% from the previous month and 3.1% annually. Both readings were in line with economists’ forecasts. Fed officials generally view core inflation as a better indicator of longer-term price pressures, although they monitor both measures. Inflation remains significantly above the Fed’s 2% target, even as the economy continues to demonstrate resilience. ## Economic growth exceeds expectations The Commerce Department report showed that US gross domestic product increased at a seasonally adjusted annualised rate of 3.4% in the third quarter, beating the 3.1% estimate and accelerating from 2.2% growth in the second quarter. Consumer spending, a key driver of the US economy, increased 0.5% in September, slightly below the 0.6% gain forecast by economists. Personal income rose 0.2%, compared with expectations for a 0.3% increase. The combination of firm economic growth and persistent inflation could make it harder for policymakers to justify easing monetary policy in the near term. The data arrived a day after the Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate in a range of 3.75%-4.00%. Officials have said they can assess incoming economic information before deciding on their next move, despite inflation remaining elevated. “The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that’s happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it,” Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said. Thursday’s figures, however, suggest that policymakers may have more work to do to bring inflation under control while sustaining economic growth.

items.title: New Releases on Netflix This Week and Top 10 Movies & Series: November 8, 2026
items.excerpt: Another Sunday roundup, but it’s well worth the wait, as this was one of the busiest weeks Netflix has had in a while. In total, 73 new movies and series hit the US library between November 1st and November 8th, headlined by the ambitious Colombian limited series Under Siege and the long-awaited second season of Black Doves, plus two of 2026’s best-reviewed smaller theatrical releases making their streaming debuts. Elsewhere, Netflix’s 2026 holiday slate officially kicked off with A Dog’s Perfect Christmas (here’s our full rundown of every new Netflix Christmas movie coming this year), Mike Tyson returned to the stage with a new one-man show, and a whopping 17 Telugu movies landed on the service in one go. --- ### Best New Movies and Shows on Netflix This Week #### Under Siege (Limited Series) Netflix Original Type: Series Genre: Historical Drama | Episodes: 8 | Language: Spanish ... Netflix’s biggest Colombian swing since One Hundred Years of Solitude arrived on Friday, and it’s no coincidence it landed on November 6th. That’s the anniversary of the 1985 siege of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá, when M-19 guerrillas seized the courthouse and the army’s retaking of the building left at least 94 people dead or missing, including Supreme Court justices. Known as Palacio in its native Colombia, the eight-part series comes from Dynamo (the same company behind One Hundred Years of Solitude) with Natalia Santa serving as showrunner and Jayro Bustamante (La Llorona) among its directors. Natalia Reyes, Carlos Manuel Vesga, and Robinson Díaz lead the cast. What sets it apart from the inevitable Narcos comparisons is that it doesn’t stop when the shooting does — a big chunk of the series follows the victims’ families over the next two decades as they fight for answers. For more, here’s our full preview of Under Siege. --- #### Black Doves (Season 2) Netflix Original Type: Series Genre: Spy Thriller | Season: 2 Netflix had so much faith in Joe Barton’s spy thriller that it renewed it before season one had even premiered, and nearly two years on, Helen and Sam are finally back. Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, and Sarah Lancashire all return for a new season that, unlike the first, has ditched the Christmas setting. The new season only dropped on Thursday, so it’s had just a few days to make its mark in the top 10s (it debuted at #12 on our weekly chart), but expect it to climb considerably next week. If you need a refresher on where we left off, our Black Doves season 2 guide has you covered. --- #### Gail Daughtry and the Celebrity Sex Pass Type: Movie Genre: Comedy | Language: English If you’ve been missing the days of gloriously dumb R-rated studio comedies, David Wain (Wet Hot American Summer, Role Models) has you covered. Co-written with his longtime collaborator Ken Marino, the film premiered at Sundance back in January before Sony Pictures Classics picked it up and gave it a theatrical run this summer. Zoey Deutch plays Gail, a small-town Kansas hairdresser whose fiancé cashes in his “celebrity pass” with Jennifer Aniston. To even the score, Gail heads to Hollywood to track down her own pass, Jon Hamm, kicking off a Wizard of Oz-style odyssey through LA packed with celebrity cameos and, for some reason, a group of Italian assassins. Miles Gutierrez-Riley, Ben Wang, John Slattery, and Marino round out the cast. It’s uneven, it’s crude, and it’s frequently very funny. ... #### Carolina Caroline Type: Movie Genre: Romantic Crime Thriller | Language: English Samara Weaving has quietly become one of the most reliable leads around, and this lovers-on-the-run thriller from Adam Carter Rehmeier (Dinner in America, Snack Shack) is a strong showcase for her. After premiering at TIFF in 2025, it got a limited theatrical release via Magnolia Pictures back in June, so plenty of people will be catching it for the first time here. Weaving plays Caroline Daniels, who’s stuck caring for her father in a small town until a charming con man (Kyle Gallner, Strange Darling) gives her a way out. The pair hit the road across the American Southeast, leaving a trail of crimes behind them as they search for Caroline’s estranged mother. Kyra Sedgwick and Jon Gries co-star, and the film comes with a great country soundtrack featuring Chris Stapleton, Jason Isbell, and Loretta Lynn. Critics have praised Weaving and Gallner’s chemistry in particular.
